places.quote: North India Revealed
Embark on a 22-day odyssey through India’s intoxicating north.
See towering sandstone fortresses, pilgrims praying on riverbanks, Maharajah mementos in a ghostly palace, and silhouettes on a desert landscape.
From the beating heart of Delhi to the holy city of Varanasi – this is north India.
From the beating heart of Delhi to the holy city of Varanasi – this is north India.
If you arrive in Delhi with time to spare before the meeting, consider finding your feet with an Urban Adventure.
The Hidden Gems of Delhi tour offers something a little different from the standard itinerary, taking you to sights most tourists never see.
Experience the chaos of an Indian traffic jam as you inch your way through the streets around Chandni Chowk marketplace in a traditional cycle rickshaw.
Visit the Jama Masjid, Delhi's oldest mosque, then stop by the Sheeshganj Gurudwara (Sikh Temple) to learn about the religion.
Visit the Jama Masjid, Delhi's oldest mosque, then stop by the Sheeshganj Gurudwara (Sikh Temple) to learn about the religion.
Visit the Jama Masjid, Delhi's oldest mosque, then stop by the Sheeshganj Gurudwara (Sikh Temple) to learn about the religion.
Tonight, transfer to the railway station and board an overnight train to Bikaner.
Bikaner a city in Rajasthan still displays its ancient opulence through palaces and forts, built of red sandstone that have withstood the passage of time.
In the afternoon relax or opt to visit Junagarh Fort: Built in 1588 AD by Raja Rai Singh.
In the afternoon relax or opt to visit Junagarh Fort: Built in 1588 AD by Raja Rai Singh.
Day 4  Bikaner to Jaisalmer
On arrival, choose whether to relax or join the group on an optional trip to the Jaisalmer Folklore Museum.
You can also find a series of Jain temples dating from the 15th and 16th centuries within the walls of the fort, and it’s easy to spend a few hours admiring their elaborate carvings.
Day 6  Thar Desert
Meet your local guides, who will cook a traditional Rajasthani dinner with chapati, dal, rice and veggies while you sit back, relax and watch the sunset.
Day 7  Jodhpur
Today you have the option to visit the colossal Mehrangarh Fort, one of the largest in India.
If you’d prefer to see a more down to earth kind of Rajasthani life, it is also possible to spend today touring nearby Bishnoi villages.
Day 9  Udaipur
This romantic city is set amid the Aravalli Hills and curls around Lake Pichola, a man-made lake created in the 14th century.
This romantic city is set amid the Aravalli Hills and curls around Lake Pichola, a man-made lake created in the 14th century.
Perhaps take a short boat ride on the famous Lake Pichola (seasonal) and see the palaces of Jag Mandir and Jag Niwas rise out of the water and their own reflections.
Perhaps take a short boat ride on the famous Lake Pichola (seasonal) and see the palaces of Jag Mandir and Jag Niwas rise out of the water and their own reflections.
Maybe you’d like to visit Sajjan Garh (Monsoon Palace), a 19th-century palace perched on a hill overlooking Lake Pichola.
Maybe you’d like to visit Sajjan Garh (Monsoon Palace), a 19th-century palace perched on a hill overlooking Lake Pichola.
Named after Maharana Sajjan Singh of the Mewar Dynasty, Sajjan Garh offers ridiculously great views of the city below.
Named after Maharana Sajjan Singh of the Mewar Dynasty, Sajjan Garh offers ridiculously great views of the city below.
Or perhaps you’re more inclined to visit the nearby village of Shilpgram, an ethnographic museum and arts hubs where traditional crafts are sold, and artists perform.
Day 11  Pushkar
Transfer to the station and travel by train for around 5.5 hours to the city of Ajmer.
Early morning risers can choose to hike up the hill to the Savitri Temple for sunrise views over the town.
Later in the day, maybe pay a visit to the colourful Brahma Temple, which is dedicated to the Hindu god.
If you’ve planned your tour to coincide with the Pushkar Camel Fair (which changes each year), today will mainly be set aside to experience one of India’s most famous festivals.
Day 13 Jaipur

This tour includes a visit to the market and opt to visit the beehive-like Palace of the Winds (Hawa Mahal), built in 1799 so that women of the royal family could observe street festivities without being seen by the public.

This tour includes a visit to the market and opt to visit the beehive-like Palace of the Winds (Hawa Mahal), built in 1799 so that women of the royal family could observe street festivities without being seen by the public.
If you’d prefer to stay grounded (but still like expansive views) the Amber Fort is both an excellent example of Rajput architecture and a great place from which to see the surrounding area.
If you’d prefer to stay grounded (but still like expansive views) the Amber Fort is both an excellent example of Rajput architecture and a great place from which to see the surrounding area.
For a true local experience, tonight you could immerse yourself in Bollywood with a movie at a classic cinema.
Day 15  Abhaneri
Visit the Chand Baori, a 20-metre-deep stepwell where water was collected and locals used to gather to escape the heat.
Next visit another jewel of Abhaneri, the Harshat Mata Temple.
Day 16  Fatehpur Sikri – Agra
Day 16  Fatehpur Sikri – Agra
Rich in Mughal heritage, Agra is a city of gardens, temples, and open rooftops.
On arrival visit the Taj Mahal, a white marble mausoleum built by Emperor Shah Jahan as a memorial to his wife Mumtaz.
On arrival visit the Taj Mahal, a white marble mausoleum built by Emperor Shah Jahan as a memorial to his wife Mumtaz.
On arrival visit the Taj Mahal, a white marble mausoleum built by Emperor Shah Jahan as a memorial to his wife Mumtaz.
One of the New Seven Wonders of the World, the Taj Mahal attracts over three million visitors each year, so be prepared for crowds.
If you’re after a cool drink or a light meal, maybe head to Sheroes Hangout.
This cafe is staffed by survivors of acid attacks and is located 10 minutes’ walk from the Taj.
While you’re here, be sure to visit the spectacular Red Fort on the banks of the Yamuna River.
Built in 1565 by Emperor Akbar, the fort was originally designed to be a military structure.
If you have extra time, you may like to continue onto Akbar's Mausoleum to pay your respects to the great emperor.
This evening, there are two options you should consider, both centred around the holy Ganges.
If you’d prefer to stay on land, you could watch local priests perform a Ganga aarti (fire ceremony) at the Dashashwamedh Ghat.
If you’d prefer to stay on land, you could watch local priests perform a Ganga aarti (fire ceremony) at the Dashashwamedh Ghat.
You could even continue your stroll to the sinking Vishnu temple near the Manikarnika Ghat.
You could even continue your stroll to the sinking Vishnu temple near the Manikarnika Ghat.
Perhaps ask your leader about how to visit Sarnath, about ten kilometres outside of the city, where Gautama Buddha is said to have given his first speech after finding enlightenment.
Perhaps ask your leader about how to visit Sarnath, about ten kilometres outside of the city, where Gautama Buddha is said to have given his first speech after finding enlightenment.
Perhaps visit the Vishwanath Temple, or simply grab some chaat and watch the world go by.
If you’re craving a little peace and quiet before you board another overnight train, consider heading to the Kriti Gallery to check out some contemporary work by local artists.

places.quote: Lower Dolpa Trek – 19 days
The Lower Dolpa Trek is an extraordinary adventure that delves into one of Nepal’s most remote and untouched regions.
The trek provides a fascinating blend of dramatic scenery, high-altitude terrain, and traditional Tibetan-influenced communities.
The journey typically begins with a flight from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj, followed by another flight or a lengthy drive to Juphal, the starting point of the trek.
The journey typically begins with a flight from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj, followed by another flight or a lengthy drive to Juphal, the starting point of the trek.
The journey typically begins with a flight from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj, followed by another flight or a lengthy drive to Juphal, the starting point of the trek.
One of the key highlights of the Lower Dolpa Trek is the exploration of Shey Phoksundo National Park.
A visit to the lake also includes exploring the surrounding areas, such as the impressive Phoksundo Waterfall, one of the highest in Nepal.
The Lower Dolpa region is also rich in cultural heritage.

Whether you’re drawn to the allure of Shey Phoksundo Lake, the challenge of high-altitude trekking, or the chance to experience traditional Tibetan culture, the Lower Dolpa Trek offers an exceptional and memorable adventure in the heart of the Himalayas.
Trek along the scenic Bheri River corridor, passing charming villages, terraced fields, gorges, and suspension bridges
Explore Tarakot — an ancient fortress village with deep historical roots as a strategic stronghold
Trek through forested trails of wild roses and juniper bushes to reach Dho Tarap — a historic trade hub between Tibet and the Mustang Kingdom

places.quote: K2 BC Concordia Trek via Gondogoro La
K2 BC Concordia Trek via Gondogoro La
Take on one of the most epic and demanding treks on earth — a 20-day odyssey through the Karakoram's crown jewels via the legendary Gondogoro La high pass.
Journey deep along the mighty Baltoro Glacier through a corridor of soaring granite towers to reach Concordia, the breathtaking amphitheater of 8,000m giants.
Journey deep along the mighty Baltoro Glacier through a corridor of soaring granite towers to reach Concordia, the breathtaking amphitheater of 8,000m giants.

Stand at K2 Base Camp, pay tribute at the Gilkey Memorial, then push higher over the formidable Gondogoro La at 5,610m — one of the world's most spectacular high-altitude crossings — descending through wildflower meadows and cedar valleys to Hushe.

Day 11: Concordia – Broad Peak BC (4850m)

The trip itself is one of the most fantastic you can make – starting in the heart of China travel to Lhasa; city of colour and life – monasteries, teahouses, markets and people.

All day the views are of the great Himalayan range to the south and, to the north, the vast dry Changtang Plateau (which turns briefly and stunningly green with the summer monsoon) and which is home to nomads whose lifestyle remains almost unchanged by the centuries.
Sacred to Buddhist, Bonpo, Hindu and Jain; every year it receives thousands of pilgrims from all corners of Tibet and India.

After 4 hours we reach Tamdin (4780m) where nomad tents serve a simple lunch and boiled water.
From here it is only 4km to Dirakpuk monastery, but this stretch has the some of the best scenery of the entire kora.

Day 3 Explore Tiananmen Square, the Forbidden City and Hutongs, train to Xi'an
From here enter the Forbidden City (built 1406-1420), the ceremonial and political center of the Chinese government for more than 500 years.
From here enter the Forbidden City (built 1406-1420), the ceremonial and political center of the Chinese government for more than 500 years.
It was declared a World Heritage Site in 1987 and is listed by UNESCO as the most extensive collection of preserved ancient wooden structures in the world.
• Overnight on soft sleeper train Beijing-Xi’an (1 night)
Day 4 Xi'an - Terracotta Warriors, Muslim Quarter

This incredible archaeological find, discovered in 1976, comprises more than 6,000 warriors, chariots and horses - each individually sculpted from clay with different costumes, height and even facial expressions – all in battle formation.

This incredible archaeological find, discovered in 1976, comprises more than 6,000 warriors, chariots and horses - each individually sculpted from clay with different costumes, height and even facial expressions – all in battle formation.
3 main pits displaying over 2,000 of the warriors are open for you to view.
3 main pits displaying over 2,000 of the warriors are open for you to view.
After lunch in a local village visit one of the best-preserved old residences in Xi’an dating back 400 years.
• Manxin Hotel Bell Tower or similar ( 2 nights)
Day 5 Train to Lhasa
It is the highest railway in the world, crossing the high altitude Changtang Plateau – the highest pass is 5069m.
The whole trip from Xi’an takes about 31 hours.
• Overnight on train Xi’an-Lhasa (1 night)
Day 6 Across the Tibetan Plateau to Lhasa
• Shang Bala Hotel or similar (3 nights)
Day 7 Jokhang Temple, Sera Monastery
• Shang Bala Hotel or similar (3 nights)
Day 8 Lhasa Potala Palace
Perched 130meters above the city, it is divided into two parts, the White Palace (secular) and the Red Palace (religious - home to chapels, shrines, and tombs of Dalai Lamas).
• Shang Bala Hotel or similar (3 nights)
Day 9 Lhasa/Gyantse -- Khambala Pass, Yamdrok Lake, Karola Pass, Gyantse Dzong
From the top of the Khamba-la (4750m) the views of the beautiful turquoise lake, Yamdrok Tso, are superb.
Descent to skirt the lake before climbing again to the Karo-la (5045m) for a close-up view of NojinGangzang glacier.
• Gyantse Hotel or similar (1 night)
Day 10 Pelkor Choede Monastery, to Shigatse, Tashilumpo

Within the complex stands Gyantse Kumbum (meaning 100,000 images), it is an eight-story structure containing a seemingly endless series of tiny chapels full of Buddhist images – Buddhas, demons, protectors, and saints.
• Tangka Hotel Shigatse or similar (1 night)
Day 11 Shigatse/Sakya/Lhatse – drive Shigatse to Lhatse via Sakya Gompa
It is about 3 hours to the Tibetan town of Sakya; site of Sakya Gompa and birthplace of the Sakya-pa sect of Tibetan Buddhism and very distinctive in its colouring.
It is also known as the “second Dunhuang,” for its huge collection of over 40,000 volumes of sacred Buddhist scripts, and just one single, long bookshelf holds around 10,000 ancient scriptures.
It is also known as the “second Dunhuang,” for its huge collection of over 40,000 volumes of sacred Buddhist scripts, and just one single, long bookshelf holds around 10,000 ancient scriptures.
• Vienna Hotel or similar (1 night)
Day 12 Lhatse to Saga
It is about 4.5 hours drive to Saga.
Arrive early in the afternoon to the typical Chinese and Tibetan town of Saga (4640m).
• Saga Yalong Zangbu Hotel or similar (1 night)
Day 13 Saga/Darchen-driving west, first views of Mt Kailash & Lake Manasarovar
From the lake several prominent peaks are visible, including Gurla Mandata (7694m).
We will continue to drive to Darchen (4675m), a small town and the starting point of the Mt Kailash kora.
• Chengbao Hotel Darchen or similar (1 night)
Day 14 Kailash Kora - Trek to Dirapuk Monastery
After 4 hours we reach Tamdin (4780m) where nomad tents serve a simple lunch and boiled water.
After 4 hours we reach Tamdin (4780m) where nomad tents serve a simple lunch and boiled water.
From here it is only 4km to Dirakpuk monastery, but this stretch has the some of the best scenery of the entire kora.
Dirakpuk (5210m), located on the north side of the Lha-chu River facing the north face of Mt.
Kailash was rebuilt in 1985.

Day 15 Kailash Kora - Trek from Dira Phuk to Zutrul Puk Monastery
Today is the most challenging part of the kora as we cross the Drolma-la (5630m).
• Zutrul Puk Guesthouse (1 night)
Day 16 Kailish Kora - Trek from Zutrul Phuk to Darchen, Drive to Lake Manasarovar
• Guesthouse Manasarovar ( 1 night)
Day 17 Lake Manasarovar/Saga - return journey across the Tibetan Plateau
• Saga Yalong Zangbu Hotel or similar (1 night)
Day 18 south across the grasslands towards the Himalaya, Rombuk & Everest Views
The world’s highest monastery, at 5000m, was first built in 1902 by a Nyingma Lama and originally housed more than 500 monks.

Day 19 Rombuk/Kyirong - Tasuwa border
Today is another long days’ drive of 350km.
It will take 6-7 hours to get to Kyirong where we spend the night before crossing the border to Nepal.

Day 20 Kyirong-Rasuwa, to Kathmandu
• Mulberry Hotel or similar (1 night)

places.quote: Khustai National Park day tour
Khustai National Park is located 120km from Ulaanbaatar city amongst the mountains that maintain their natural beauty, unharmed by human activities.
Nowadays, it is best known as the sanctuary for Przewalski Wild Horses which are also known as ‘Takhi’ in Mongolian.
Nowadays, it is best known as the sanctuary for Przewalski Wild Horses which are also known as ‘Takhi’ in Mongolian.
These wild horses, native to Mongolia, went extinct by the year 1954.
However, thanks to efforts spearheaded by the Dutch, these horses were reintroduced to their native habitat in the early 1990s.

places.quote: Ghorepani Poonhill Trek
Mesmerizing View from the Poonhill
Mesmerizing View from the Poonhill
The Ghorepani Poonhill Trek stands out as one of Nepal’s most favored short treks.
Situated in the Annapurna region, it is renowned for its vibrant Rhododendron forests that add a brilliant touch to the trail in spring.

This trek is especially celebrated for its iconic viewpoint at Poonhill, offering stunning sunrise vistas and a sweeping panoramic view of the Himalayan ranges including majestic peaks like Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, Hiun Chuli, Dhampus Peak, Nilgiri, and Machhapuchre.

Thailand conjures up images of spicy delicacies, majestic elephants, golden Buddhas, colourful hilltribe villages, fantastic shopping and exotic hideaways - and we experience it all on this trip.

Witness traditional hilltribe life in a H'mong village, support the rehabilitation of the endangered Asian elephant, step back in time in the ancient kingdom of Sukhothai and try your hand at creating some gastronomic delights.

Embark on a scenic, winding drive up a mountain (approximately 45 minutes) to one of the country's most stunning temple complexes, Doi Suthep.

Set in a peaceful valley of a scenic mountain range and surrounded by stunning natural landscapes of jungle with misty mountain views, the Hmong lodge offers a unique and tranquil experience.
The Hmong are an ethnic minority in Thailand who originated in the south of China.

This morning you’ll get an insight into the darker side of Kanchanaburi’s history with a moving visit to the Hellfire Pass Memorial, built to honour the Allied POWs and Asian conscripts who died while constructing some of the most difficult stretches of the Thai-Burma Death Railway.

Day 2 – Bangkok - Overnight Train To Chiang Mai
Begin the day with a river cruise down the Chao Phraya River to explore the famous ‘khlongs’ (canals) (approximately 1 hour).
Day 3 – Chiang Mai
Embark on a scenic, winding drive up a mountain (approximately 45 minutes) to one of the country's most stunning temple complexes, Doi Suthep.
A 300-step naga-guarded stairway leads you to the temples, and the climb is well worth the effort.
Day 4 – Chiang Mai
Day 5 – Chiang Mai - Hmong Lodge
Board a minivan for the drive north to the Hmong Hilltribe Lodge, set in picturesque hilly countryside (approximately 1.5 hours).
Day 6 – Hmong Lodge - Sukhothai
Depart the hilltribe village this morning and head on to Lampang (approximately 2 hours).
After spending time with the elephants, farewell your new pachyderm pals and head to Sukhothai (approximately 3.5 hours) for the night.
Day 7 – Sukhothai - Kanchanaburi
Located on a fertile plain, Sukhothai was established in the 13th century as one of the first ancient capitals of Siam, and the name means the 'Dawn of Happiness'.

The religious art and architecture of the Sukhothai era are considered to be the most classic of Thai styles, and the Sukhothai Historical Park contains the remains of 21 historic sites, with awe-inspiring Buddha images and four large ponds often filled with stunning lotus flowers in full bloom.
You’ll then hop on a private minibus south to Kanchanaburi (approximately 6 hours).
Day 8 – Kanchanaburi
You can head out to a teak observation deck and look across to Myanmar just 25 miles away.
You’ll also see the eponymous pass, cut through rock 18 metres deep, that got its name from the hellish fires used to light the work at night.
Day 9 – Kanchanaburi - Bangkok
Return to the bustling capital Bangkok by private minivan today (approximately 3 hours).
Day 10 – Bangkok - Departure
